short: the planner's price for a plan, in made-up units where one page read in order is 1.0. compared between plans, never a time.
the price of one page read as part of a sequential run. 1.0 by default, the unit every other cost is measured in.
the price of one page read out of order, as an index scan does. 4.0 by default; about 1.1 is common on SSDs.
the price of handling one row in a plan node. 0.01 by default, next to cpu_index_tuple_cost (0.005) and cpu_operator_cost (0.0025).
how much of the database the planner may assume is cached. not memory it allocates: an input to the index scan's cache model.
one way to produce a table or a join (a seq scan, an index scan, a hash join), with its cost. the planner keeps the cheapest ones.
the readable view of the statistics ANALYZE collects: one row per column, from the pg_statistic catalog.
the command that samples a table and writes its per-column statistics. autovacuum runs it after 50 + 10% of the rows change.
how detailed column statistics are: up to this many MCVs and histogram buckets, from a sample of 300 times this many rows. 100 by default.
the fraction of a column's rows that are NULL, in pg_stats.
the number of distinct values in a column. negative means a fraction of the row count: -1 is unique.
a column's most common values and the fraction of rows each one has, in pg_stats. equality on one of them is estimated exactly.
bounds that cut a column's non-MCV values into buckets holding the same number of rows. range estimates interpolate inside a bucket.
from -1 to 1, how closely a column's order matches the rows' physical order. near 1 or -1 makes index scans cheap.
the rows= a plan node expects to return: a selectivity times the table's row count, before anything runs.
the fixed guess the planner uses when no statistics apply: 0.005 for =, 1/3 for <, 0.005 for a range.
the planner multiplies the selectivities of conditions on different columns, as if they were unrelated. correlated columns break it.
a row estimate far from the actual count (10x is the usual alarm). low in a plan, it compounds into bad join choices above.
statistics on a combination of columns or an expression, declared with CREATE STATISTICS: dependencies, ndistinct, mcv.
which tables are joined first. n tables have n! left-deep orders; postgres searches them with dynamic programming over sets of tables.
how many explicit JOIN items the planner reorders at once (8). at 1, joins happen in the order written. from_collapse_limit is its twin for FROM lists.
the genetic query optimizer: a randomized join order search used from geqo_threshold (12) items, faster and not always the best plan.
merging a subquery in FROM into the outer query, so its tables and conditions are planned together. LIMIT, aggregates and OFFSET 0 prevent it.
a subquery the planner couldn't turn into a join, run per outer row; hashed when its result fits in work_mem. an InitPlan runs once.
a plan for a prepared statement made for the actual parameter values. the first five executions always get one.
a plan for a prepared statement made for any value ($1 in EXPLAIN). used from the sixth execution if it's not dearer than the custom plans.
auto, force_custom_plan or force_generic_plan: whether prepared statements may switch to a generic plan.
an extension that totals calls, rows, time and pages per normalized statement. needs shared_preload_libraries.
a module that logs the plan of any statement slower than auto_explain.log_min_duration, as it actually ran.
switches like enable_seqscan and enable_hashjoin. off doesn't forbid: postgres 18 avoids disabled nodes and prints Disabled: true when it can't.
an extension that reads planner hints from comments. core postgres has no hints.
